title: UConn Overwhelms Georgia Tech for Second Title
dek: Emeka Okafor's 24 points and 15 rebounds powered UConn past Georgia Tech, 82-73, for its second national title in six seasons, a night before the UConn women won theirs.

setup.text: Four months earlier, Georgia Tech had knocked top-ranked UConn from No. 1 with a 77-61 win in the Preseason NIT semifinals at Madison Square Garden. That night Okafor was fighting back spasms, Charlie Villanueva had not yet been cleared to play, and Will Bynum was not yet eligible for the Yellow Jackets.

Picked to finish seventh in the ACC, Georgia Tech reached its first title game by winning four of its five tournament games by 5 points or fewer; the other was an overtime win over Kansas in the regional final. Bynum's driving layup with 1.5 seconds left beat Oklahoma State in the semifinals.

UConn (32-6) had survived its own scare, erasing an eight-point deficit in the final three minutes against Duke. On the morning of the final, Jim Calhoun learned he had not been elected to the Basketball Hall of Fame; he missed by one vote.

Two Georgia Tech regulars, B.J. Elder and Isma'il Muhammad, were playing hurt; Elder had scored 2 points since spraining an ankle. The New York Times' William C. Rhoden called UConn the overwhelming favorite.

game.text: Josh Boone's free throw and Rashad Anderson's 3-pointer opened the scoring for UConn. B.J. Elder's 3 pulled Georgia Tech within 9-7, and Luke Schenscher's layup made it 11-9.

The marquee matchup inside belonged to Okafor, who used his strength against the 7-foot-1 Schenscher. He had 10 points and 7 rebounds by halftime, and Schenscher picked up his second foul reaching over him with about six minutes left in the half.
Georgia Tech missed 24 of its 34 first-half shots, and UConn turned all six of the Yellow Jackets' first-half turnovers into 12 points.

sequence.text: Clarence Moore's layup puts Georgia Tech ahead 12-11. It will be the Yellow Jackets' only lead.
Okafor's jumper puts UConn back in front, for good.
Schenscher is called for fouling Ben Gordon on a 3-point attempt, a call that angers Georgia Tech coach Paul Hewitt. Gordon makes all three free throws.
Josh Boone scores on a layup.
Gordon hits another 3, his third. He has 12 points barely 10 minutes in.
Will Bynum's 3 pulls Georgia Tech within 10. The Yellow Jackets will not score again in the half.
Bynum misses two free throws. Okafor grabs the rebound and fires it ahead to Anderson, whose pull-up from the top of the key beats the horn. After a replay review, it counts as a 2.
Taliek Brown grabs a defensive rebound and pushes ahead to Okafor. Okafor misses, and Boone follows for a 25-point lead.
Okafor nudges Schenscher aside for an offensive rebound and scores on a short hook over him.
Georgia Tech hits four 3-pointers in the last 44 seconds and gets within seven, but the horn sounds on an 82-73 UConn win.

quotes.text: After we are long dead and gone, we're still going to have this championship banner. We immortalized ourselves.
Just proves we are as good as everybody originally said we were.
quotes.role: UConn junior center, Final Four Most Outstanding Player

quotes.text: Going wire-to-wire is one of the hardest things you can do, and it wasn't just the beginning of the year for us.

quotes.when: postgame, after the nets came down

aftermath.text: Okafor was named the Final Four's Most Outstanding Player, and Gordon and Anderson joined him on the all-tournament team. The win was Calhoun's 680th, and it made him one of three active coaches with more than one national title, with Mike Krzyzewski and Bob Knight.

Former Huskies including Ray Allen, Richard Hamilton and Kevin Freeman celebrated on the Alamodome floor. Back home, police arrested 35 people as celebrations near campus spilled into fires and two overturned cars off campus.

The next night in New Orleans, the UConn women beat Tennessee 70-61, making UConn the first Division I school to win both basketball titles in the same season. A joint parade in Hartford on April 18 drew an estimated 250,000 to 300,000 people, which police called the city's biggest public event since the veterans parades after World War II.

On May 19, President George W. Bush honored the team at an East Room ceremony for four NCAA champions. Okafor, who earned his degree in three years, and Gordon went No. 2 and No. 3 in the 2004 NBA draft.

legacy.text: UConn became the first preseason No. 1 to win the title since Kentucky in 1996, and joined Duke and Kentucky as the only programs with more than one title since the field expanded to 64 teams in 1985.
It was the second of the six national championships listed in UConn's record book.

conflicts.source_says: Contemporaneous sources: 44,468 (Courant box and story; Ticker box via USA Today; ESPN box). UConn's record book lists 44,147 in its 2003-04 season log and 44,417 (the semifinal figure) in its largest-crowds list. Draft uses 44,468. Settled: 44,468 is correct. It is the figure in the NCAA's official attendance history and in every contemporaneous box (ESPN box via Wayback 2005, Ticker, Courant). The record book's 44,147 (season log) and 44,417 (largest-crowds list) are errors: the book repeats one figure for both Final Four games in each list. 44,417 is the semifinal crowd, and 44,147 looks like a transposition of it.

Ticker (USA Today) calls it a 3-pointer at the buzzer. ESPN play-by-play lists a 2-point jumper, the CBS broadcast shows officials reviewing and counting it as a 2, and the score went from 39-26 to 41-26.
Ticker (USA Today): 'for a 21-12 advantage with 11:18 left before halftime.'
